title: Compatible product of completed polynomial fibres
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be Noetherian local commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $B$ a finite $A$-algebra. Let $q\subset A[X]$ be maximal with $q\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$, let $r\subset A[X]$ and $s\subset B[X]$ be prime [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and let $L$ be a field equipped with $\kappa(r)$- and $B$-algebra structures. Suppose $e:\kappa(s)\cong L$ is a $B$-algebra isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] such that for every $f\in A[X]$, the image under $e$ of its coefficientwise image in $\kappa(s)$ equals its image under $A[X]\to\kappa(r)\to L$. Put $C=(A[X]_q)^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There exist $n\ge0$ and maximal ideals $q_i\subset B[X]$ for $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, each contracting to $\mathfrak m_B$ and containing $s$, with a ring isomorphism $L\otimes_{\kappa(r)}(\kappa(r)\otimes_{A[X]}C)\cong\prod_i(\kappa(s)\otimes_{B[X]}(B[X]_{q_i})^\wedge)$. The empty product is the zero ring. All types have one common universe.

proof.text: Polynomial coefficient extension is finite: use polyEquivTensor, tensor commutativity, and Module.Finite.base_change. Apply completion_finite_extension_decomposition at q to obtain finiteness of Q = q.primesOver B[X] and the B[X]-algebra equivalence C tensor B[X] with the product of completed localizations. The extra completed localized tensor equivalence of completion_finite_extension is not used.
Each prime over q is maximal by integrality. Its contraction in B is prime over the maximal ideal of A, hence maximal by integrality of A to B and therefore the maximal ideal of the local ring B.

Equip L with the A[X]-algebra structure through kappa(r) and the B[X]-algebra structure through e. The equation he supplies the scalar tower and an A[X]-algebra equivalence er from kappa(s) to L. Compose cancelBaseChange, congr er, cancelBaseChange in reverse, commRight, tensor congr of the completion decomposition, and piRight. This gives the ring equivalence with the product of all s-fibres. The finite-product module equivalence of tensor-finite-product is used in its right-handed algebra form Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight; multiplicativity is built into that Mathlib equivalence.

For t in Q with s not contained in t, choose x in s outside t. IsLocalization.map_units and the completion algebraMap make x a unit in D(t). Its image in kappa(s) is zero, so includeRight carries that unit to zero in s.Fiber D(t). Hence zero equals one and this fibre is subsingleton. Restriction of products to U = {t in Q | s is contained in t} is injective by those subsingleton instances and surjective by extending by zero. Form its RingEquiv.ofBijective and reindex by (Fintype.equivFin U).symm. The inherited primesOver.isMaximal instances and the contraction calculation supply all ideal clauses. No nonemptiness is assumed for U.
